data.title: From 2017 crackdown to UN court, a decade of the Rohingya crisis
data.description:
The United Nations' highest court for disputes between states, the International Court of Justice (ICJ), will rule on Thursday in a landmark case accusing Buddhist-majority Myanmar of committing genocide against the minority Rohingyas, who are mostly Muslim.

More than one million Rohingya refugees who fled Myanmar currently live in Bangladesh, most of them in the Cox's Bazar district, according to the UN.

Here is a timeline of events in the Rohingya crisis:

Aug 25, 2017 - The Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA), a Muslim militia, attacks 30 police posts and a military base in Myanmar's Rakhine State.

Aug 26, 2017 - Thousands of Rohingya people flee across the border into Bangladesh as clashes between Myanmar's military and ARSA intensify.

Sept 2, 2017 - More than 2,600 houses are razed in Rohingya-majority areas in the week following the Aug. 25 attack according to the Myanmar government.

Sept 11, 2017 - The U.N. human rights high commissioner calls the military operation "a textbook example of ethnic cleansing".

Sept 19, 2017 - Myanmar leader Aung San Suu Kyi pledges to hold those behind rights abuses to account, but makes no mention of U.N. accusations of ethnic cleansing.

Dec 12, 2017 - Medecins Sans Frontières publishes survey results from Rohingya refugee camps in Bangladesh that say at least 6,700 Rohingya, in the most conservative estimations, were killed between August 25 and September 24, including at least 730 children below the age of five years.

Jan 10, 2018 - The military admits its soldiers killed 10 detained Rohingya at Inn Din village. Seven soldiers are sentenced in April 2018 but released early in May 2019.

Nov 11, 2019 – Predominantly Muslim Gambia files a genocide case against Myanmar at the International Court of Justice, accusing it of atrocities against the Rohingya.

Dec 11, 2019 - Aung San Suu Kyi appears before the ICJ in The Hague and rejects genocide allegations as "incomplete and misleading."

Jan 23, 2020 – The ICJ orders Myanmar to take urgent measures to protect Rohingya people who remain in the country.

Feb 1, 2021 – Myanmar's military stages a coup, arrests Aung San Suu Kyi and overthrows the elected government, sparking nationwide conflict.

July 22, 2022 – The ICJ rejects objections raised by Myanmar and rules it has jurisdiction under the Genocide Convention and that Gambia's application is admissible.

Jan 12, 2026 - Myanmar targeted minority Muslim Rohingya for destruction and made their lives a nightmare, Gambia tells ICJ judges, as public hearings on the merits of the case begin.

Jan 16, 2026 - Myanmar tells the ICJ that Gambia has not proven the Rohingya genocide case, following a statement by the foreign ministry that terms the allegations by Gambia as "flawed and unfounded in fact and law."

Nov 3, 2026 – The ICJ announces it will deliver its judgment on Nov. 19.

data.title: European Shares Likely To Open On Firm Note Ahead Of Anthropic Debut
data.description:
BRUSSELS/FRANKFURT/PARIS (dpa-AFX) - European stocks may open on a firm note on Thursday after Anthropic's IPO raised $81.31 billion, surpassing SpaceX's reported $75 billion offering and pushing the company's valuation beyond its earlier target of $1.4 trillion.

U.S. stock futures ticked higher ahead of Anthropic's debut on stock markets.

Investors also seek cues from weekly jobless claims data due later in the day as well as earnings from Walmart and Gap.

Asian markets were mostly lower as investors weighed a sharp selloff in commodities, AI-related financial risks and hawkish Fed signals.

The U.S. dollar retreated from a near 20-month high in Asian trading. Gold prices edged up 0.2 percent to $3,732 an ounce after falling more than 3 percent to its lowest level since September 2025, pressured by a stronger dollar and hawkish Fed remarks.

Brent crude futures were little changed around $92 a barrel, trading near their lowest levels since late August as IEA projections of a sizeable oil market surplus into 2027 and data showing a larger-than-expected build in U.S. crude and fuel inventories outweighed renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

U.S. stocks ended mostly lower overnight amid concerns over elevated valuations of AI-related stocks and expectations of prolonged monetary tightening.

The minutes of the Fed's October policy meeting showed nearly all officials had agreed they would likely have to raise interest rates 'in the months ahead'.

Two officials said a rate increase exceeding 25 basis points could warrant consideration in December if inflation continues to run hotter than expected.

With inflation heading in the wrong direction and spreading out, the Fed has to unwind the trio of quarter-point cuts it made last year, and possibly go beyond that, Fed Governor Waller told CNBC.

The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.4 percent as Nvidia's strong earnings lifted tech stocks.

The S&P 500 dropped 0.2 percent to reach a three-month closing low while the narrower Dow tumbled 1.1 percent to hit a five-month low.

European stocks ended sharply lower on Wednesday, with weak commodity prices and hot eurozone and U.K. inflation data weighing on sentiment.

The pan-European STOXX 600 fell 1 percent to extend losses for a third consecutive session. The German DAX dipped 1.2 percent, France's CAC 40 fell 0.9 percent and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 declined 1.3 percent.

data.title: City Union Bank shuts NEFT, RTGS gateway after unauthorised transaction
data.description:
City Union Bank informed exchanges on Thursday of an incident involving an unauthorised NEFT transaction in one of its customer accounts on November 16, 2026.

“Immediately upon becoming aware of the incident, we have taken the necessary steps to investigate and respond to the incident, including shutting down the NEFT and RTGS gateway pertaining to the respective customer’s account,” the bank said.

The private bank is also working with experts to support the investigation, he added.

No material impact on business operations

“We submit that the bank does not have any material impact of this incident on its core business operations, financial performance or business continuity,” the bank said.

The bank stressed that its core business functions continue to operate normally without disruption. “The bank continues to monitor the situation closely and take all appropriate measures in accordance with the applicable statutory and regulatory requirements.”

The matter is being analysed to ascertain the root cause, and necessary corrective measures are being undertaken; hence, this disclosure is being made to the exchange today.

data.title: Palm slides nearly 3% on weak Dalian palm olein
data.description:
Malaysian palm oil futures slid nearly 3% on Thursday, extending losses to a third straight session, as Dalian palm olein tumbled on record high inventories in China.

The benchmark palm oil contract for February delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange slid 108 ringgit, or 2.46%, to 4,278 ringgit ($1,040.12) a metric ton by the midday break.

The market came under heavy selling pressure in tandem with weakness in Dalian palm olein and soyoil as bearish sentiment swept across the broader edible oil complex, a Kuala Lumpur-based trader said.

Anilkumar Bagani, head of research at vegetable oil broker Sunvin Group, said that the selloff in Dalian palm olein futures has been staggering this week as the market is feeling the heat from the historically high palm oil stocks there.

"Prices are under pressure too as the narrowing discount against gasoil threatens demand for palm oil in biofuel production," he said.

Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) fell 1.25%, while its palm oil contract shed 4.06%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade were up 0.05%.

Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.

Crude oil prices steadied after losses in the prior session as expectations for a market surplus outweighed lingering worries about Middle East supply amid attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. O/R

Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.

The ringgit , palm's currency of trade, weakened 0.02% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly cheaper for buyers holding foreign currencies.

($1 = 4.1130 ringgit)

data.title: Maybank Likely to Post 3.3% Higher Third-Quarter Profit — Earnings Preview
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong

Malayan Banking is scheduled to report its third quarter results on Monday. Here's what you need to know:

NET PROFIT FORECAST: Maybank is expected to record quarterly net profit of 2.71 billion ringgit, equivalent to $663.2 million, according to the consensus estimate of eight analysts in a Visible Alpha poll. That would be a 3.3% increase from 2.62 billion ringgit a year earlier and 0.7% higher than 2.69 billion ringgit in the second quarter.

NET INTEREST INCOME: Quarterly net interest income likely climbed 20% to 3.92 billion ringgit in the third quarter, from a year ago, according to Visible Alpha.

Maybank's shares have fallen 6.2% over the past three months, pressured by rising bond yields amid a more hawkish Federal Reserve outlook, which has heightened concerns over funding costs and net interest margins. The planned expansion of the Kuala Lumpur Composite Index to 50 constituents from 30, aimed at reducing the index's concentration in financial stocks, has also weighed on sentiment toward the bank.

WHAT TO WATCH:

  • NET INTEREST MARGIN: Net interest margin could remain under pressure as rising deposit competition drives up funding costs ahead of any benefit from a potential Bank Negara policy rate hike, Hong Leong Investment Bank analyst Raymond Ng said in a note. Maybank guided a 25 basis point rate hike could eventually lift NIM by 1-3 basis points, but Ng expects the benefit may be limited by deposit competition and the pace of funding-cost repricing.
  • CAPITAL ADEQUACY: Maybank's capital buffer could face greater pressure from rising bond yields. A 100 basis point rise in bond yields could reduce Maybank's bank-level capital ratio by 104 basis points, RHB Investment Bank analysts David Chong and Tan Yenn Lynn said in a note. Maybank may need to maintain its dividend reinvestment plan to preserve capital, they added.

Write to Ying Xian Wong at yingxian.wong@wsj.com

data.title: Stocks of Diageo, other liquor makers fall in India on Scotch tariff jolt
data.description:
Key points:
  • Importers of Scotch in India fall in morning trade
  • Pernod and Diageo shares fall in Paris and London
  • Higher levy could hit margins and working capital, ICICI Securities says
  • Britain says ministers are urgently working with India to resolve dispute

By Aditya Kalra

Shares of Scotch and whisky sellers in India including Diageo's local unit fell on Thursday after Reuters reported that New Delhi is imposing levies of 162.5% on bulk Scotch imports, in the first major dispute under the India-UK trade agreement.

The India-UK trade pact, which came into effect in July, halved tariff rates on Scotch to 75% and was seen as a big win for firms like Pernod Ricard , owner of Britain-based Chivas Brothers, and Diageo . The companies import bulk Scotch and blend it with other spirits to sell popular brands in India's $65 billion market.

India has started applying total duties of 162.5%, partly payable via bank guarantees, a rate higher than the 150% levy that was in place before the pact kicked in. New Delhi has asserted that bulk Scotch is merely a raw material for other products and doesn't qualify for lower tariffs under the India-UK pact.

Shares of Indian companies that import bulk Scotch to make popular whiskies fell on Thursday. United Spirits , Diageo's Indian unit, fell more than 4% in early trading before paring some losses.

Rival Radico Khaitan also fell around 3.5% while Allied Blenders and Distillers dropped more than 2%.

In a recent investor presentation, Allied Blenders said it is “one of the largest bulk Scotch importers” and the trade pact ​would improve its “luxury portfolio accessibility."

Diageo declined to comment on the 162.5% tariff and tax, while the other companies mentioned in this article did not respond to requests for comment.

MODI MEETS PRINCE, PRINCESS OF WALES

Pernod, which counts India as its biggest market by volume, is not listed in India, but its shares in France, and Diageo's in London, both fell after the Reuters story on the 162.5% levies was published on Wednesday.

The higher levy could weigh on liquor makers' profitability, reversing anticipated margin benefits from lower import costs under the trade agreement, ICICI Securities said in a research note.

"It will put stress on margins and working capital," ICICI said.

On Wednesday night, reacting to the Reuters story, the British government said ministers are working with ​India to resolve the ‌dispute over tariffs.

This week, Britain's Prince William and Kate, Princess of Wales, were in India and met Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday at the end of their three-day visit.

In a statement, the Indian government said Modi welcomed growing momentum on Indian-British relations, adding that the "meeting also provided an opportunity to exchange views on further strengthening" the trade agreement. The statement did not say if the Scotch dispute was discussed.

data.title: The Adecco Group global study: AI delivers more value when people are involved in work redesign
data.description:
New research among 40,500 workers finds well-integrated AI saves more time, while training, worker involvement and human-centered leadership determine whether adoption translates into sustainable performance.

  • AI delivers greater value when it is embedded into how work gets done. Workers using well-integrated AI save 20% more time per day and are more likely to reinvest that time in higher-value work.
  • Worker involvement turns adoption into adaptability. 96% of workers involved in redesigning their work are willing to adapt to changing environments, compared with 29% of those not involved.
  • Work-life balance has overtaken salary as the leading reason people would leave their job. It is now workers' leading reason for considering a move.

ZÜRICH, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Adecco Group () today published the seventh edition of its annual Global Workforce of the Future report, based on a survey of 40,500 workers across 36 countries. The findings show that AI adoption is advancing rapidly, but technology delivers its strongest value when organizations redesign work around people; equip them with relevant skills; and give them a voice in how change is implemented.

AI is now embedded in working life. Nearly three-quarters (74%) of workers use AI agents at work, up from 64% in 2025, and technology occupies four of the five leading influences reshaping work. Yet adoption alone does not guarantee value. The research points to a widening gap between organizations that simply deploy AI and those that orchestrate people, AI agents and workflows as a well-orchestrated hybrid workforce.

Where AI is well integrated into operating workflows, workers report saving 20% more time per day than users experiencing lower integration. They are also more likely to reinvest the time saved in higher-value work and seven times less likely to feel overwhelmed by the need to use AI tools effectively. The findings suggest that productivity gains depend less on access to technology than on how effectively it is embedded into the work itself.

Denis Machuel, CEO of the Adecco Group: "The next phase of AI at work is not about deploying more tools. It is about orchestrating people and technology more effectively. When workers help redesign how work gets done, and receive the training and clarity to adapt, AI creates more value and change becomes easier to navigate. AI delivers its greatest impact when it happens with people and not to people."

data.title: Anthropic’s Cash Pile Tops Amazon And Nvidia Combined After Record IPO – Meet The New ETF Tracking ANT-Linked Companies
data.description:
Key points:
  • Anthropic's post-IPO cash position will increase to $237.2 billion from $131.8 billion.
  • Anthropic raised $81.34 billion in a fresh issue and another $26 billion through a private placement with select investors.
  • Anthropic priced IPO shares at $83, sharply higher than its previously indicated range.

Anthropic on Wednesday priced its IPO well above its previously indicated range, raising a staggering $107.3 billion including the private placement – making it the largest IPO in history in a resounding vote of confidence for the AI trade.

The IPO puts Anthropic right up in the elite tech league. Based on the $83 IPO price, Anthropic would now have a cash position bigger than Amazon (AMZN) and Nvidia (NVDA) combined and just below thrice as much as Meta Platforms’.

Including the $26 billion private placement, Anthropic's post-IPO cash position will increase to $237.2 billion from $131.8 billion. The figure includes cash, cash equivalents and securities, and short-term investments. It is below only Berkshire Hathaway (BRK) and Alphabet (GOOGL).

The blockbuster IPO from Anthropic is a strong vote of confidence in the AI industry, signaling that investors believe the technology’s growth justifies enormous capital commitments. Anthropic’s listing on Thursday would likely boost the sentiment for AI-linked companies from chipmakers and data-center operators to cloud and software companies.

The IPO was oversubscribed nearly seven times and drew roughly $500 billion worth for orders, Bloomberg reported. Anthropic raised a total of $107.34 billion, including the $81.34 billion in fresh issue and $1.96 billion by selling shareholder stock.

 Number of sharesAmount

Offer for sale (Class A shares)23,648,646$1.9 billion

Source: Anthropic filings

With the cash bank filled up massively, investors would find some comfort in Anthropic’s ability to meet its staggering $900 billion spending plan that had raised eyebrows previously.

The company has said it will rely on AI sales and cash proceeds to meet those obligations. Anthropic has purchase contracts with several important players such as Amazon, Google, Nvidia, Micron and others.

Harbor Capital's ANTW ETF Offers Another Way To Play Anthropic

On Wednesday, Harbor Capital launched the Harbor Anthropic AI Lab Ecosystem ETF (ANTW) which aims to invest in the companies the fund believes are most directly linked to Anthropic.

In a factsheet, Harbor said ANTW’s top five holdings are Terawulf (WULF), Amazon, Alphabet, Broadcom (AVGO) and Riot Platforms (RIOT).

“There's a lot of focus on $ANT's potential IPO but its S-1 also shows hundreds of billions in planned spending on chips and compute,” Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities, said in an X post.

“That's what makes the idea behind $ANTW interesting because the companies supplying Anthropic could benefit from that spending regardless of how the stock itself performs.”

data.title: Missed the RIL rally? JPMorgan sees another 23% upside, highlights two key triggers
data.description:
Shares of Reliance Industries Ltd. have gained over 13% in the past month and could see further gains as improving earnings momentum, particularly in its oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business, supports its outlook, according to JPMorgan's latest note on Thursday, November 19.

The global investment firm has maintained its "Overweight" rating on the stock with a price target of ₹1,675, implying an upside potential of around 23% from Wednesday's closing price of ₹1,363.

JPMorgan sees two key factors shaping the stock's outlook: the earnings recovery and the valuation support following its recent rally.

The firm expects Reliance Industries to report strong year-on-year growth in net profit over the next few quarters, supported by the O2C business. It also sees scope for further earnings upgrades, particularly for financial year 2028, if margins remain firm.

JPMorgan believes the stock has not fully reflected the earnings upgrades already made by analysts, suggesting that there could be further room for the share price to catch up with improving estimates.

However, the recent rally has also reduced the valuation discount that Reliance offered in October. The decline in comparable valuations for its retail business has further narrowed the discount available to investors. While the stock's price-to-earnings multiples relative to the broader market remain supportive, JPMorgan believes further gains may require fresh triggers.

These could include an improvement in the performance of the retail business, some signs of which are expected in the December quarter, or the commencement of renewable energy installations, which the firm sees as likely between March and June 2027.

Reliance Industries Q2 performance

Reliance Industries reported its strongest-ever quarterly performance in the September quarter, with consolidated net profit rising 33.8% year-on-year to a record ₹29,550 crore. Revenue increased 27.8% to an all-time high of ₹3.62 lakh crore.

Consolidated earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) grew 23.9% to a record ₹62,409 crore, while profit before tax rose 32.6% to ₹38,613 crore. The company's first-half net profit crossed ₹50,000 crore for the first time.

The O2C business was a key contributor, with revenue rising 44.2% to ₹2.32 lakh crore and EBITDA increasing 67.9% to a record ₹25,203 crore. Its EBITDA margin expanded to 10.9% from 9.3% a year earlier, supported by higher product prices and stronger transportation fuel cracks.

Analyst consensus and stock performance

Reliance Industries shares are a consensus "buy" among all 33 analysts who cover the Nifty 50 heavyweights. The consensus estimates of price targets implies an upside potential of 16% from current levels.

Shares of Reliance Industries are trading 0.3% lower on Thursday at ₹1,359. The stock broke it’s 12 session-winning streak on Wednesday to end 0.3% lower. The shares had gained close to 17% over the 12 sessions. The stock still trades lower on a year-to-date basis.

data.title: IIFL Finance shares drop over 3% after Fairfax pared over 13% stake
data.description:
Shares of IIFL Finance declined over 3 per cent on Thursday, a day after domestic and global institutional investors, led by SBI Mutual Fund, Rimco India and Goldman Sachs, picked up a 13.24 per cent stake in the firm from Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa's Fairfax group.

The stock dropped 3.15 per cent to ₹641 despite a positive beginning to the trade on the BSE. At the NSE, it fell 3.24 per cent to ₹640.50, erasing early gains.

Domestic and global institutional investors, led by SBI Mutual Fund, Rimco India and Goldman Sachs, have picked up a 13.24 per cent stake in IIFL Finance for ₹3,488 crore from the Fairfax group, which is moving towards a complete exit from the non-banking financial company.

The investors collectively acquired over 5.65 crore shares of Mumbai-based IIFL Finance through open market transactions on Wednesday, according to block deal data on the BSE.

SBI Mutual Fund emerged as the largest buyer, purchasing 81.53 lakh shares or nearly 2 per cent, for ₹503.04 crore.

Mauritius-based fund Rimco India Ltd followed, acquiring more than 60.77 lakh shares, representing a 1.42 per cent stake, for ₹375 crore.

Nippon India Mutual Fund bought shares worth ₹275 crore, while Goldman Sachs, through its affiliates, acquired shares worth ₹180.22 crore.

Other buyers included mutual funds managed by Aditya Birla Sun Life, HDFC, Franklin Templeton, Axis and Edelweiss, along with insurers such as ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, Kotak Mahindra Life Insurance and Tata AIG General Insurance.

On the selling side, Fairfax's arm FIH Mauritius Investment offloaded over 5.65 crore shares in 39 tranches at the same price, as part of its strategy to completely exit IIFL Finance.

After the latest transaction, Fairfax's holding in IIFL Finance has reduced to 0.4 per cent from 13.64 per cent.

data.title: India’s companies rank 4th globally with $3.76 trillion in intangible assets
data.description:
India’s listed companies hold an estimated $3.76 trillion in intangible assets, making the country the fourth-largest market globally, according to the Global Intangible Finance Tracker (GIFT) 2026 report by brand valuation consultancy Brand Finance.

Intangible assets account for 68 per cent of the enterprise value of Indian companies, exceeding the share in major Asian economies.

Intangible assets are identifiable, non-monetary assets without physical substance and can be broadly categorised into rights (leases, agreements and contracts), relationships (including a trained workforce), and intellectual property (brands, patents and copyrights).

In India, such assets account for 68 per cent of the $5.49 trillion enterprise value analysed, exceeding the corresponding shares in South Korea (62 per cent), China (60 per cent) and Japan (49 per cent).

Nearly 65 per cent of India’s enterprise value consists of undisclosed intangible assets, including brands, technology, intellectual property and customer relationships that are not fully reflected on corporate balance sheets.

Several companies recorded strong gains in intangible value across infrastructure, financial services and consumer sectors. Adani Power’s intangible value increased 76 per cent, while Bajaj Auto and State Bank of India registered gains of 40 per cent and 25 per cent, respectively.

“India’s economy has long been driven by services and intellectual capital. With the corporate landscape evolving, and encouragement from the local government for manufacturing investments in semiconductors, mobile manufacturing and renewable energy infrastructure, opportunities for creating intangible value are emerging across multiple sectors,” said Ajimon Francis, Managing Director, Brand Finance India.

At the company level, Reliance Industries remains India’s most valuable company by intangible asset value, at $135.8 billion, followed closely by Bharti Airtel at $131.4 billion.

However, both companies dropped out of the global top 100 after ranking 82nd and 94th, respectively, in 2025. The threshold for entry into the list rose to around $164 billion, highlighting the increasingly competitive landscape among the world’s most intangible-asset-rich companies.

Uphill IT climb

Indian IT services companies are facing pressure amid AI-driven disruptions reshaping the global technology industry.

According to Francis, the race to lead AI transformation is pushing Indian companies to move beyond traditional service offerings and create proprietary intellectual property, enabling them to convert investments in brands and intangible assets into sustainable, market-recognised value.

“Stronger management and reporting of these assets will be essential to long-term competitiveness,” he said.

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and Infosys reported declines in intangible value of 31 per cent and 32 per cent, respectively.

This stands in contrast to developments elsewhere in Asia, where China’s intangible asset value rose 85 per cent and Japan’s increased 75 per cent, supported in part by growth in AI- and semiconductor-related businesses.

data.title: Asian Equities Mixed Amid Cautious Market Sentiment — Update
data.description:
By Ronnie Harui and Megan Cheah

Asian equities were mixed Thursday afternoon as expectations for higher interest rates and renewed concerns over technology stocks kept investors cautious.

Investors digested a hawkish tone struck in minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting while awaiting a summit between President Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"Trump and Xi are also scheduled for a separate bilateral meeting. The meetings represent the highest-level diplomatic engagement in months and will be closely watched for any signals on trade, technology restrictions, and the broader geopolitical framework affecting Asian markets," Commerzbank Research analysts said.

Anthropic's trading debut was also in focus as a test of investor appetite for artificial-intelligence stocks after the Nvidia scandal triggered another wave of selling in the technology sector.

Concerns over tighter U.S. export restrictions on advanced chips continued to weigh on Asian technology and AI-related stocks.

Taiwan's Taiex fell 3.4%, while Chinese benchmarks also declined. In Hong Kong, losses in major technology stocks dragged both the Hang Seng Index and the Hang Seng Tech Index down 2.0%.

South Korea's Kospi recovered earlier losses and was last up 0.3%. Tourism stocks rallied after South Korea and China substantially concluded negotiations to expand their free-trade agreement to cover services and investment, including tourism and financial services.

The development also raised hopes that China could ease its unofficial restrictions on South Korean pop culture, lifting entertainment stocks.

Japan's Nikkei Stock Average fluctuated between gains and losses and was last 0.45% higher.

Elsewhere, crude-oil futures were mixed after Iran launched attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain on Wednesday and continued targeting ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil shipments.

Front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures edged down 0.25% to $83.05 a barrel, while Brent crude oil futures rose 0.15% to $92.09 a barrel, ICE data showed.

Gold reversed earlier gains, slipping 0.1% to $3,723.42 an ounce.

data.title: India's ArMee Infotech signs solar agreement
data.description:
ArMee Infotech (BSE: 544951) has signed a memorandum of understanding with Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company (MSEDCL) for a 135 MW solar power project in the western Indian state, the company said in a stock exchange filing on November 17.

The deal carries an aggregate order value of INR16.29bn ($174.421mn). According to the filing, under the agreement, ArMee MH ONE Renewable Energy, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Mumbai-listed company, will execute a power purchase agreement with the state-run distribution utility to build the solar plant.

The filing did not give a timeline for construction or the tariff at which power would be sold. The company described the order as domestic. It said neither its promoters, promoter group nor group companies hold any interest in MSEDCL.

The contract will not be treated as a related party transaction. ArMee Infotech made the disclosure under Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India's rules on listing obligations and disclosure requirements, which oblige listed firms to report material contracts to the exchanges. Company Secretary and Compliance Officer Purnima Jain signed the filing. The company said the notice would also be posted on its investor relations website.

data.title: Intel lands first external customer for 18A-P chips
data.description:
Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said on Wednesday that the company has signed the first outside customer for its 18A chips. INTC shares rose 2.6% in extended trading.

“Resilient supply on the foundry is very important,” Tan said at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Texas, according to CNBC. “And then 18A, I’m involved in production and we just signed the first customer,” Tan added, without naming the debut client.

It’s a milestone moment for Intel in its five-year effort to take on chip manufacturing leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing . “It’s a huge win for foundry,” Creative Strategies analyst Ben Bajarin told CNBC in an interview.

Pushkar Ranade, Intel’s technology chief, clarified on X that the external customer had signed up for Intel’s 18A-P manufacturing process node, which went into risk production in June. In May, reports indicated that Apple and Intel were closing in on a deal to use Intel’s foundry to make some of the chips for Apple devices.

Earlier this month Intel shareholders sued the company for allegedly misleading investors about the impact that a slowdown in personal ​computer sales had on its Q3 results, which caused its stock to plunge nearly 29% in a single day.

data.title: Lenovo posts 48% revenue jump on AI-related sales, beating estimates
data.description:
By Che Pan and Eduardo Baptista

China's Lenovo reported a 48% jump in second-quarter revenue, beating analyst estimates, on strong growth in AI-related sales such as servers and other hardware.

Here are some key financial data :

  • Revenue rose to $30.2 billion, above an LSEG consenus estimate of $27.6 billion drawn from six analysts.

  • Under Hong Kong accounting standards (HKFRS), the company posted a net loss of $640 million, compared with a net profit of $340 million a year earlier.

  • But Lenovo also said that it booked, under different accounting standards, adjusted net profit of $1.4 billion, up 166%. The adjusted figure strips out non-cash accounting items linked to warrants and convertible bonds that Lenovo issued as part of its strategic partnership with Alat, a manufacturing and technology company in Saudi Arabia.

  • The Infrastructure Solutions Group, which makes servers and data center equipment, had its strongest quarter ever, with revenue climbing 178% year-on-year to $11.3 billion.

  • AI-related revenue rose 79% to $10.8 billion, comprising 36% of the group's total revenue.

  • Lenovo’s PC, tablet and smartphone division, which accounted for about 60% of total revenue during the quarter, grew 15%.

data.title: Taiwan's Delta Electronics looks to triple India revenue in 4-5 years on AI boom
data.description:
By Praveen Paramasivam

Taiwan's Delta Electronics aims to at least triple its India revenue over the next four to five years as global investment in AI data centres accelerates, a senior executive at the power and cooling systems supplier told Reuters.

India is emerging as Asia's fastest-growing data centre market, with capacity set to more than triple by 2029, requiring $110 billion in investment, according to property consultancy JLL India.

"We would like to achieve a growth of at least three times what we are in the next four to five years, because we see a good market or good pull from the AI data center industry, where we are heavily present," Delta Electronics India Managing Director Niranjan Nayak said.

Total revenue at the company rose 16% to 37.61 billion rupees ($402.38 million) in fiscal 2025, while net profit climbed 12% to 1.37 billion rupees, according to Tofler data. Delta did not disclose its India revenue.

Nayak said demand from AI data centres, electronics and semiconductor manufacturing, energy projects, electric vehicles and buildings would drive growth.

Delta, which partners with Nvidia on data centre projects globally and supplies major cloud providers, expects its India data centre and telecom business to contribute 50%-55% of revenue within four to five years, up from 40%-42%, as it expands manufacturing capacity.

Stronger-than-expected demand has also accelerated hiring. Delta's India workforce has surpassed 5,000, and Nayak expects headcount to grow about 15% annually over the next two to three years.

In September 2024, another Delta executive had said the company planned to add 3,000 employees over five years to its then workforce of 3,500.

($1 = 93.4700 Indian rupees)

data.title: KKR Invests in Gentari’s Renewables Platform in India
data.description:
Clean energy solutions company Gentari and leading global investment firm KKR today announced that capital accounts advised by KKR have made a minority investment in Gentari Renewables India Pte Ltd, which holds Gentari’s renewables platform in India. ​​The investment will provide growth capital to support the platform’s continued expansion in the country.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261118076160/en/

India remains a key market for Gentari, underpinned by increasing renewable energy demand, supportive market fundamentals and long-term opportunities. The investment marks an important milestone in the evolution of Gentari’s renewables platform in the country. Today, Gentari's India platform has approximately 8 GW of operating, under-construction and contracted renewable energy capacity, with a robust development pipeline. The platform serves commercial and industrial customers, as well as government entities, through a diversified portfolio spanning solar, wind, hybrid and battery energy storage solutions, helping meet India’s growing clean energy needs. This reflects Gentari’s progress in scaling the business into one of its largest growth platforms. The strategic partnership with KKR brings together Gentari's development, execution and operating capabilities with KKR’s long-term investment and deep infrastructure experience to support the platform’s next phase of growth.

Sushil Purohit, Group Chief Executive Officer, Gentari, commented, "This strategic partnership reflects confidence in the scale and maturity of the platform we have built in India as well as the strength of our growth trajectory. We are pleased to welcome KKR as an investor, given its long-term investment approach and deep experience supporting infrastructure and energy businesses globally. With KKR’s support, we are well-positioned to continue scaling the business as a self-sustaining renewable energy platform focused on long-term value creation."

Hardik Shah, Partner, Asia Pacific Infrastructure, KKR, said, “India’s demand for reliable power is growing rapidly, creating a significant need for continued investment in the country’s energy infrastructure. We believe scaled platforms that can deliver increasingly sophisticated renewable energy solutions will have an important role to play in meeting that demand. Gentari has built strong capabilities across renewable generation, hybrid solutions and energy storage and we look forward to supporting the business in its next phase of growth.”

KKR has been investing in India’s infrastructure sector for more than a decade, with a focus on building and scaling platforms across sectors including renewable energy, power transmission, roads, logistics and transportation. In renewable energy, KKR has invested in Serentica Renewables and Hero Future Energies, building on KKR’s broader approach of supporting and scaling infrastructure platforms in India. Since 2011, KKR’s infrastructure platform has committed more than US$27 billion in energy transition and renewables infrastructure globally.

Following the investment, Gentari will continue to retain strategic oversight and operational control of the platform in India. This milestone reinforces Gentari's long-term commitment to India and supports the next phase of expansion of its renewables platform in the country.

As part of the PETRONAS Group, Gentari is a clean energy solutions company operating across Renewable Energy, Hydrogen and Green Mobility. Through these businesses, Gentari supports customers in addressing evolving energy needs while balancing energy security, reliability, and affordability. With 9.1 GW of renewable energy capacity installed and under construction globally, Gentari has established a growing presence across key markets including Malaysia, India and Australia. Its renewable energy portfolio spans solar, onshore and offshore wind, and battery energy storage, while its hydrogen and green mobility businesses continue to expand. Gentari is also advancing cross-border energy initiatives, including renewable electricity interconnection opportunities in Southeast Asia. By combining expertise across its businesses, Gentari helps customers optimise energy systems, strengthen operational resilience, and create long-term value. Gentari aims to be Asia Pacific's most valued clean energy solutions partner. For additional information, visit www.gentari.com.

data.title: Australian Dollar Slides as Thoughts Turn to RBA Rate Cuts
data.description:
By James Glynn

SYDNEY--The Australian dollar weakened after news the country's unemployment in October surged to its highest level since 2021.

The Aussie fell to around 66.60 U.S. cents after the data was released early Thursday, hitting its weakest levels since January, from around 67.20 U.S. cents just prior.

Economists were surprised by a rise in unemployment to 4.9% in October from 4.7% in September, which brought with it a fall in employment of close to 50,000 jobs over the month.

The data immediately cast doubt on whether the Reserve Bank of Australia would be able to raise interest rates further, after delivering five increases since the start of the year.

To be sure, the discussion in financial markets also turned more fully to the question of when the RBA might start cutting interest rates.

Interest rate swap markets had been pricing a 28% chance of an interest rate rise by February. After the data, that shifted to a 20% chance of an interest rate cut by March.

An interest rate cut by November next year is now fully priced in.

Taylor Nugent, an economist at National Australia Bank, said unemployment is already well above where the RBA had expected it to be in the final months of the year, which supports the case that the interest rate tightening cycle is over.

NAB expects the RBA will start cutting interest rates in August next year as the economy slows and inflation pressures ease.

Currency traders are weighing competing influences as it was only on Tuesday that RBA Governor Michele Bullock reaffirmed her view that inflation risks remain skewed to the upside.

Bullock said the problem with inflation is that it isn't just due to high oil prices, adding that domestic price pressures are also strong, fueled in part by a boom in data center investment.

Also, wages in the third quarter grew at their fastest pace in three years, something that will further stoke fears at the RBA that high inflation expectations are becoming embedded.

Inflation data for October will also be published next week with economists fearing that it could bring more bad news for the RBA.

The central bank recently forecast that inflation won't return to the target of 2.5% until mid-2028, leaving it open to a lot of forecast error.

Still, traders are now more comfortable about ruling out a further interest rate rise by the RBA.

"The weaker-than-expected jobs data reinforces our view, and market expectations, that the RBA's tightening cycle is over and its next move will be a rate cut," said Carol Kong, currency strategist at the Commonwealth Bank of Australia.

CBA is now forecasting two interest rate cuts in August and November, she added.

"The dovish repricing of RBA policy has pushed Australian dollar back to where it started the year. We continue to see the path of least resistance for the currency as lower over the coming months," Kong added.

  • Write to James Glynn at james.glynn@wsj.com

data.title: Senators warn GENIUS Act rules could push stablecoin firms toward federal oversight
data.description:
Six bipartisan senators on Tuesday urged the US Treasury Department to extend proposed regulatory protections to state-supervised stablecoin issuers, warning that proposed GENIUS Act rules could steer firms toward federal licenses.

In a letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Senators Cynthia Lummis and Kirsten Gillibrand, along with Angela Alsobrooks, Kevin Cramer, Pete Ricketts and Mark Warner, said Treasury’s proposal offers a safe harbor to certain issuers with pending federal applications and regulator-approved waivers, but no equivalent protection for state issuers.

The senators warned that issuers “may be incentivized to seek greater operational clarity under a federal license,” including through the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), which they said was “the opposite of our intent in drafting this legislation.”

The senators urged Treasury to extend the safe harbor to issuers in states expected to have qualifying frameworks in place before Jan. 18, 2028, reducing uncertainty while certification reviews are pending.

The senators’ request follows a June appeal, urging Treasury to preserve state participation and clarify the certification process.

The GENIUS Act generally allows issuers with $10 billion or less in outstanding stablecoins to operate under qualifying state supervision, with exemptions available above that threshold.

Kevin Wysocki, head of policy at Anchorage Digital, questioned whether a broader safe harbor would make much difference. He said issuers are choosing federal oversight because they risk having to switch regulators if their stablecoins exceed $10 billion in circulation, although exemptions are available.

data.title: Copper price hits 7-month low: Voltas, PG Electroplast, Blue Star shares rally up to 7% on input cost relief hopes
data.description:
Shares of air-conditioning and cooling products manufacturers witnessed significant rally in today’s trading session, November 19, as copper prices tumbled to their lowest level in seven months, raising expectations of lower input costs and improved margin prospects for companies engaged in the sector.

On Wednesday, copper prices slipped to 7-month-low as a stronger US dollar, growing concerns over Chinese industrial demand and a selloff in AI-related stocks overshadowed tightening supplies of the metal.

Three-month copper futures on the London Metal Exchange fell 4.6 percent to $12,471.00 a metric ton, the lowest settlement since April 7. Front month copper fell 5.3 percent in New York to $5.6595 a pound, also the lowest since April 7, reported WSJ.

AC stocks buz in today’s trade on likely input cost benefits

Stocks such as Voltas, Blue Star, PG Electroplast and Amber Enterprises India rallied up to 6 percent during the session, on optimism over the potential benefits of easing raw material costs.

Voltas and PG Electroplast were leading the gains. Shares of Voltas rallied opened at Rs 1,133.20 and rallied 6.6 percent to touch an intra-day high of Rs 1,207.45 from its previous close of Rs 1,132.10. At around 10.47 am, the stock was trading 6.8 percent higher at Rs 1204.35, on the BSE.

Shares of PG Electroplast opened at Rs 539.15 and climbed as much as 6 percent to an intra-day high of Rs 570.75 from its previous closing of Rs 538.25. At around 10.47 am, the stock was trading 5,42 percent higher at Rs 567.40, on the BSE.

Shares of Blue Star opened at Rs 1,620 and surged 5.5 percent to hit an intra-day high of Rs 1,708 compared with the previous closing of Rs 1,618.30.

Shares of Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals opened at Rs 208.85 and gained 4.7 percent to touch an intra-day high of Rs 216.75 from the previous closing of Rs 207.

Meanwhile, shares of Amber Enterprises India Ltd opened at Rs 6,253.90 and rallied 3.6 percent to hit an intra-day high of Rs 6,451, compared with the previous closing price of Rs 6,222.20.

data.title: Malaysia's Stronger 3Q Growth Unlikely to Prompt Bank Negara Rate Hike — Market Talk
data.description: Malaysia's stronger-than-expected 3Q GDP growth is unlikely to materially raise the probability of a Bank Negara Malaysia rate increase in January 2027, CIMB economists Chew Khai Yen and Michelle Chia say in a note. Private consumption growth has moderated, while uneven services activity and easing services inflation point to limited demand-driven price pressures, they say. BNM is likely to remain focused on the inflation outlook, particularly amid upside risks from higher production costs, weather disruptions as well as coming income and wage measures, they reckon. CIMB expects 4Q GDP growth to moderate to 5.1% from 5.5% in 3Q. It raises Malaysia's 2026 growth forecast to 5.5% from 5.0%, but maintains its view that the policy rate will stay at 2.75% in January. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
